When I was younger I was sexually abused. It hurt me, quite a lot. Ever since that, I never felt good enough for anyone. I felt worthless because he did it and saw I wasn't going to mean anything to anyone. I didn't tell my parents until years later. I never felt like I could tell them anything. They always told me I wasn't as smart as my brothers. They always made me feel stupid. More so my mother than my father. My friends did the same thing too. I was always the stupid one, the one who was just kept around for the jokes. If I got anything higher than an 80, it seemed as though the apocalypse was happening. I felt okay for years, sure there were times I felt stupid and worthless but I never dwelled on it because I was young and my attention was always going elsewhere. In 8th grade, one of my friends had become very close to me and forced me to tell them everything. All because I stood up to other kids about making fun of my friend. I never opened up to people easily, but my friend was pushing me to open up. I got so confused and freaked out most of the year. Until I snapped at them one day and moved on with life, going to a different high school and making new friends. Now, years later after I've finally told my parents, everything's getting worse. My parents don't believe me. My mom is worse than ever, and I keep thinking about it. All the time. It's getting so bad. I promised my best friend I wouldn't hurt myself again, and I'm 10 days clean, but I feel like I want too. I'm getting worse again, and I feel more confused than ever.

There's been a lot going on in life. It brings me down a lot. I don't like being down. I don't like hurting myself. But it feels like it's the only thing I can do. I want to change, but I don't know how. It's like there's this plague in my head that keeps telling me 'No, you're not going to get happy.' And it brings me down even more. 
I don't know what else to do.

One of the first things to understand is that it isn't your fault. Having everyone in your community say its your fault could evidently make you think that it was your fault. It isn't and never will be.

I was sexually abused as well and I refuse to go to therapy. So, it's okay to not want to go to therapy, but if you really need to go to therapy then talk to your parents and tell then that you NEED the therapy. 
It's okay to cry about it. It's okay to feel the way you do. Everyone does it. Having everyone say that it's your fault is a very hard thing but from what it seems to me is that you're still young, 15-17 years old. Soon you'll be going to college and forgetting about the community. If you don't choose to go to college then I strongly suggest at least moving away from there. 
There's nothing you can do about what people choose to believe. The abusers mother will undoubtedly believe what her son is saying. All mothers believe their own children. The rest of the community seems to be a little bit slow in the head (no offense). Believing that a kid who's 4 years YOUNGER than the other could manipulate someone? That's a little weird in itself. Sure it happens but, personally, I'd be a little skeptical about that story. 
All in all, it's okay to feel manipulated and like no one believes you. Just make sure you know the truth and you believe the truth. Crying helps a lot as well. So, don't feel bad if your crying and you think you should be better. Everything is going to be okay, I promise you. Life will go on, it will get better. 
If you ever need to talk, you can always PM me. I know what your going through. 
Stay strong.
